title: OOP: Skill Summary
intro: Mix everything from this module: classes and instances, methods and properties, inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation and magic methods.

questions.prompt: Write `Task(title, done=False)` with `complete()` (sets done) and `__str__` returning `[x] title` when done, `[ ] title` otherwise.

tests.name: value
tests.code:
t = Task('Water plants')
assert str(t) == '[ ] Water plants'
t.complete()
assert str(t) == '[x] Water plants' and str(Task('Pay rent', True)) == '[x] Pay rent', 'Check __str__ before and after complete().'

questions.hint: A conditional expression inside the f-string picks `x` or a space.
questions.explanation: A small class with state, a method and `__str__`.

questions.prompt: An instance attribute hides a class attribute with the same name. What does this print?
questions.code:
class Config:
    mode = 'light'

a = Config()
b = Config()
a.mode = 'dark'
print(a.mode, b.mode, Config.mode)
questions.hint: Assigning `a.mode` creates an attribute on `a` only.

questions.prompt: Write a base `Shape` whose `area()` raises `NotImplementedError`, and subclasses `Circle(r)` and `Rect(w, h)` that implement it (`3.14159 * r * r` and `w * h`).

tests.name: subclasses
tests.code: assert Rect(2, 3).area() == 6 and round(Circle(2).area(), 2) == 12.57, 'Each subclass should compute its area.'

tests.name: base

questions.hint: `raise NotImplementedError` marks a method subclasses must provide.
questions.explanation: The base class defines the interface; children fill it in.

questions.prompt: Every team shares one member list, so adding to one adds to all. Fix it so each team has its own.

tests.name: value
tests.code:
a, b = Team('red'), Team('blue')
a.join('Ana')
assert a.members == ['Ana'] and b.members == [], 'Each team should keep its own members.'
tests.message: Give each team its own list.

questions.hint: A list defined on the class is shared by every instance.

questions.prompt: A `Car` has an `Engine`. Which design fits best?

options.text: Give `Car` an `engine` attribute holding an `Engine` object

questions.explanation: Composition (*has a*) fits; inheritance is for *is a* relationships.

questions.prompt: Write `Student(name, grade)` where `grade` is a property validated in its setter (0–100, else `ValueError`), plus a read-only property `passed` (grade 50 or more).

tests.name: ok
tests.code:
s = Student('Ana', 49)
assert not s.passed
s.grade = 50
assert s.passed, 'passed should follow the grade.'

tests.name: validate

questions.hint: One property with a setter, one without.
questions.explanation: Validation and derived values both live in properties.

questions.prompt: Fill in the call that runs the parent's `__init__`.

tests.name: value
tests.code: assert (tom.name, tom.indoor) == ('Tom', True), 'tom should have name and indoor.'

questions.hint: It gives access to the parent class.

questions.prompt: Write `Coordinate(lat, lon)` with `__eq__` and `__hash__` (based on the `(lat, lon)` tuple) so duplicates collapse in a set, and `__repr__` like `Coordinate(38.7, -9.1)`.

tests.name: set
tests.code:
s = {Coordinate(38.7, -9.1), Coordinate(38.7, -9.1), Coordinate(51.5, -0.1)}
assert len(s) == 2, 'Equal coordinates should collapse to one in a set.'

questions.hint: Objects that are equal must have equal hashes — hash the same tuple you compare.
questions.explanation: `__eq__` plus `__hash__` makes objects usable in sets and as dictionary keys.

questions.hint: Each object answers in its own way.

questions.prompt: A tiny library: `Book(book_id, title)` and `Library` with `add(book)`, `checkout(book_id, member)` and `return_book(book_id)`. Raise `KeyError` for unknown ids and `ValueError` when checking out a book that's already out. `available()` returns the titles not checked out, sorted.

tests.name: flow
tests.code:
lib = Library()
for i, t in [(1, 'Dune'), (2, 'Beloved'), (3, 'Emma')]:
    lib.add(Book(i, t))
lib.checkout(2, 'ana')
assert lib.available() == ['Dune', 'Emma']
lib.return_book(2)
assert lib.available() == ['Beloved', 'Dune', 'Emma'], 'checkout and return_book should update available().'

tests.name: errors

questions.hint: Keep books in a private dictionary keyed by id; a helper `_get` raises `KeyError`.
questions.explanation: Two small classes, each with a clear job, working together.
